title: Maresius and Alting: adequate object the whole Word — proper object Christ/Gospel
source_text: XXII. Similiter Maresius in Systemate docet fidei justificantis objectum adaequatum esse Dei Verbum; objectum autem proprium speciale & proximum esse doctrinam de Jesu Christo, & promissionem remissionis peccatorum in ipsius sanguine. Loco undecimo, Thesi 36. Et eodem plane modo Henricus Altingius dicit objectum fidei generatim & adaequate consideratum esse totum Verbum Dei, & quicquid in eo continetur; sed specificè & proprie consideratum objectum esse Evangelium, sive Christum Redemptorem, prout in Evangelio & Sacramentis offertur. Locor. communium parte 1. pag. 218, & 219. Quibus reliqui omnes Theologi consentiunt, nec opus est plurium testimonia congerere.
pass_a_gloss: Similarly Maresius in the System teaches that the adequate object of justifying faith is the Word of God; but the proper, special and proximate object is the doctrine of Jesus Christ, and the promise of remission of sins in His blood. Place eleven, Thesis 36. And in entirely the same way Henry Alting says the object of faith generally and adequately considered is the whole Word of God, and whatever is contained in it; but specifically and properly considered the object is the Gospel, or Christ the Redeemer, as He is offered in the Gospel and Sacraments. Common Places part 1, pages 218 and 219. With which all the remaining Theologians agree, nor is there need to heap up the testimonies of more.
pass_b_english: Maresius: adequate object = God’s Word; proper/special/proximate = doctrine of Christ and remission in His blood (XI.36).
Alting: generally/adequately = whole Word; specifically/properly = Gospel / Christ the Redeemer in Gospel and Sacraments.
The rest of the Theologians agree — no need to pile more citations.
